title: NeuroMSleepModeD Neuromodulation in patients with early stage depression and sleeping disturbances as well as multiple sclerosis
summary:
Patients with early-staged depression (and sleep disorders) as well as multiple sclerosis (MS) and depression (and sleep disorders) will receive non-invasive transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) over a four-week period. The study will examine the effects of taVNS on depressive symptoms as well as its impact on brain networks, the immune system, and sleep.
Research Questions:
What are the short- and long-term changes in the functional connectivity of neuronal networks and at symptoms within depression and sleep disorders among patients in the early stages of the disease, patients with MS, and healthy controls undergoing transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation? Patients will be recruited to perform taVNS independently, using a portable stimulator. Imaging and other examinations will be conducted at regular intervals, and questionnaire data will be collected.

interventions.name: Patients with mild to moderate early-stage depressive symptoms, four-week treatment with transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•    Mild to moderate depressive symptoms, acute depressive episode (including sleep disturbances)
•    (MS diagnosis)
•    If applicable, diagnosis of depression for no more than 4 years
Exclusion criteria:
•    Use of psychiatric medications or sedative sleep aids
•    Severe visual impairment
•    Severe physical or other psychiatric conditions
•    Alcohol or drug dependence
•    Metal objects that are not compatible with MRI scans
